response.sql: WITH grp AS (SELECT t.ordertypedist AS order_type_mix, COUNT(*) AS behavior_count FROM advancedbehavior a JOIN transactionrecord t ON a.translink = t.transreg GROUP BY t.ordertypedist), shares AS (SELECT order_type_mix, behavior_count, CAST(behavior_count AS NUMERIC) / SUM(behavior_count) OVER () AS share FROM grp), base AS (SELECT order_type_mix, behavior_count, share, AVG(share) OVER () AS baseline_share FROM shares) SELECT order_type_mix, behavior_count, share, share - baseline_share AS above_baseline FROM base WHERE share > baseline_share;

assumptions.assumption: The inner JOIN drops behaviour records with no matching transaction, and transreg is the primary key, so each behaviour record joins at most once and COUNT(*) equals the number of behaviour records per group.
A record with no mix recorded means ordertypedist IS NULL. GROUP BY places all NULL mixes in one group, which is shown as NULL. Empty strings are treated as a real mix value, not as missing.

The share is each group's count divided by the total count across all groups (after the join). The baseline is the unweighted mean of those group shares, and shares are returned at full precision with no ROUND.
